geometry.locator: Large neutrino telescope Baikal-GVD: recent status (arXiv:2309.16310)
geometry.note: 12-vertex geodesic circle approximation, radius 60 m computed on R=6371008.8 m from the centre (104.4000000, 51.7667000).
geometry.quote: Seven peripheral strings are uniformly located at a 60 m distance around a central one.

method: A 60 m radius circle centred on the surveyed site coordinate (geometry:baikal-gvd-site-point), showing the footprint of ONE Baikal-GVD cluster (not the full multi-cluster array). The status paper (arXiv:2309.16310) states a cluster's own layout directly: 'Seven peripheral strings are uniformly located at a 60 m distance around a central one. Together they form a completely functionally independent unit called cluster.' No fetched source this session states the full array's overall footprint diameter across all clusters (the same paper gives only the ~300 m hexagonal spacing between cluster CENTRES, not a bounding shape for the whole deployed array, and does not state how many clusters were in place as of the cited 2023 season in so many words -- '96 strings' divided by '8 strings per cluster' [1 central + 7 peripheral, both figures quoted in the same paper] implies 12 clusters, but that arithmetic is not itself an official statement of array extent and is not drawn as a second circle). accuracy_m is set to 2000 m to match the coarser accuracy of the site anchor point.
name: Baikal-GVD single-cluster footprint (derived circle)
notes: No checks[] row: the circle's radius IS the sourced figure (60 m string distance), so a span check against that same number would be tautological, not an independent cross-check (same reasoning as the KM3NeT/ARCA footprint, geometry:km3net-arca-footprint).

summary.plain: A schematic circle showing the 120 m width of a single Baikal-GVD cluster (one central string plus seven strings 60 m around it); the growing array has multiple such clusters spaced about 300 m apart, which are not all drawn here.
